strongest_angle: Explain the new Connecticut pay‑transparency mandate and expanded lactation‑break rules, plus the nationwide trend of fourteen states requiring salary‑range postings as of October 2026.

key_facts.fact: Effective October 1 2026, Connecticut law requires all Connecticut employers to disclose a salary range in every internal and external job posting and to create an employee guide describing pay codes.
Connecticut’s October 1 2026 amendment also expands employer obligations to provide reasonable lactation breaks for nursing employees.
As of October 2026, fourteen states and Washington, D.C. require employers to post a pay range in job advertisements.
The IRS updated the 2026 General Instructions for Forms W‑2 and W‑3, raising the maximum exclusion for employer‑provided dependent‑care benefits to $7,500 beginning with the 2026 tax year.

quotes.text: Connecticut pay transparency law and requirement to create an employee guide for pay codes effective October 1.
